name: Anglefrauding

card.summary: Choosing camera angles, distance and lighting so that a photo makes the face look better than it does in person.
card.note: Photos taken this way can differ noticeably from how a person looks in real life.

quick.overview:
Anglefrauding is looksmaxxing slang for using camera positioning to look better in photos. Changing the height of the camera, the tilt of the head, the lens distance and the lighting alters how facial features appear in a picture.

In communities, people post face photos for ratings and often mention whether the picture is angle-frauded. Threads discuss it alongside makeup as a way to present the face well [1].
quick.how: People experiment with camera height and head tilt, distance from the lens, and lighting until a flattering image results, and often pair this with makeup or grooming [1].
quick.risks: The main downside discussed is a gap between photos and real-life appearance, which can affect how ratings or first meetings in person are received. Community threads debate whether the practice is acceptable [2].

lead: Anglefrauding (also angle fraud) is a term from looksmaxxing forums for picking photo angles that present the face more favourably than a typical or neutral view would. It is widely used in rating threads, where users note that a photo is only "slightly" angle-frauded or call out photos that appear heavily so.

The appearance goal is a better-looking image: the same face can appear to have a stronger jaw, larger eyes or smoother skin depending on camera position, lens distance and lighting. Community threads link the practice to makeup as another way of managing presentation [1].
Threads on looksmax.org question whether anglefrauding is bad [2] and relate it to craniofacial structure [3]. No clinical studies address the term.

chain: Adjust camera height, head tilt, distance and lighting
Features such as jaw and eyes appear different in the image
angle.text: People use camera positioning to make photos of their face look better, often alongside makeup. The change affects the image, not the face itself.

paras: Anglefrauding refers to deliberately choosing viewpoints and poses that flatter the face. Participants in rating threads often qualify their photos with notes such as slight angle frauding so reviewers can account for it [4].

The term is used both as a self-description and as an accusation when someone's photos appear to differ from their in-person look. A thread asks whether the practice is harmful [2], and another discusses it together with makeup [1]. Opinions in these threads differ on whether it is a legitimate way of presenting oneself.

lore.intro: The practice is discussed in several looksmax.org threads, from jokes about skilled practitioners to debates over whether it is ethical [2][4].

claims.claim: Camera angle alone can change perceived facial attractiveness a lot
claims.believers: Forum users post before-and-after or angle comparisons and discuss it with makeup as a major lever on photo appearance [1].
claims.experts: No studies are cited here that measure this for the forum practice.
